sections.hypothesis: btc-regime-trend on ETH and SOL earns more with a mirror-image short side: short the coin while BTC is below its 50-day average and the coin is below its close 30 days earlier, sized as the long side is. Today it sits in cash then. Hypothetical: Kestrel can't short (P5 parked; retail shorting in Australia is CFDs at 2:1, real perps are wholesale-only). A pass is recorded as needs-shorting and never traded until a licensed retail route exists.
sections.rationale: Who pays: the same under-reaction that pays the long side, on the way down: holders who sell late (the disposition effect), and in crypto, forced selling as leveraged longs are liquidated in a falling market. Outside evidence: time-series momentum earns on both its long and short sides across 58 futures markets (Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen 2012, Journal of Financial Economics), and trend in crypto prices (Liu and Tsyvinski 2021, Review of Financial Studies). Not a rejected family: trend, the family of every pursued strategy. Disclosed: findings 16 (the overlap report) showed the pursued strategies lose a little in BTC's falling months, which is what suggested a short side; and short squeezes in crypto are violent, which is the risk this tests. Runs: one, two trials (ETH, SOL) in the main log.
sections.rules: Long side: btc-regime-trend unchanged (long while BTC closes above its 50-day average and the coin above its close 30 days earlier; size min(1, 50% / the coin's annualised volatility of its last 30 daily log returns)). Short side, its mirror: short while BTC closes below its 50-day average and the coin below its close 30 days earlier, the same size. Otherwise cash. ETH and SOL, each separately. Decide at each close, trade at the next open (the engine's convention); returns open to open, daily, 2020-01-01 to 2025-10-31 (Binance funding history starts 2020-01; nothing from the holdout). Weights in [-1, 1]: short notional never above equity, inside ASIC's 2:1 retail cap (margin 50% of notional). A short is closed out if a day's high reaches 1.5x its entry (a conservative 2:1 margin call), at that price.
sections.parameters: btc_days 50, coin_days 30, vol_days 30, target_vol_pct 50 (the pursued long rule's settings; the short side uses the same ones). Nothing else is tried; a change is a new version with a reason.
sections.costs: Long side as kestrel.toml (7.5 bps fee with the BNB discount plus the coin's half-spread band, on every change in weight). Short side, primary (the retail route: a 2:1 CFD like Eightcap's): 2x the coin's spot half-spread band on every change in short weight (CFD spreads are wider than spot; no commission) plus financing of 5% a year on short notional, charged daily (Eightcap's trade page lists a 5% p.a. BTC swap; whether that is the short rate is unconfirmed: check before freezing). Reported, deciding nothing (same signals, so not extra trials): the short as a Binance USDT-M perp (5 bps taker per side plus the band, and its real 8-hourly funding: a positive rate pays the short), and the CFD at 15% a year (an older Eightcap rate).
